scenes.heading: GitOps & Deployment Strategies
scenes.subheading: Blue-green, canary, and Git as the source of truth
scenes.narration: GitOps makes Git the single source of truth for your infrastructure, and pairs beautifully with progressive deployment strategies like blue-green and canary.

scenes.heading: The GitOps model
bullets: A controller continuously reconciles the cluster
Every change is a reviewed, auditable commit
Rollback is just reverting a commit
scenes.narration: In GitOps, the desired state of your system is declared entirely in a Git repository. A controller such as Argo CD or Flux continuously watches that repo and reconciles the live cluster toward it. Because every change is a commit, you get built-in review and a full audit trail. And rolling back is as simple as reverting a commit.

scenes.heading: Blue-green vs canary

right.label: Canary
points: Roll out as metrics stay healthy

scenes.narration: Blue-green keeps two full environments and flips all traffic from the old to the new at once, giving instant rollback by switching back. Canary instead shifts traffic gradually within one environment, sending a small percentage to the new version first and increasing it only as long as the metrics stay healthy. Blue-green is simpler; canary limits the blast radius.

scenes.heading: A canary rollout
scenes.narration: A canary rollout deploys the new version alongside the old. It routes a small slice of traffic, say five percent, to the new version. It closely watches error rates and latency during that window. If the metrics stay healthy it ramps traffic to one hundred percent, and if they degrade it automatically rolls back.

scenes.heading: An Argo CD Application
scenes.code:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: data-platform
spec:
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/acme/gitops.git
    path: envs/prod
    targetRevision: main
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: data
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
scenes.narration: This Argo CD Application points at a Git repository, a specific path, and a branch that together define the desired production state. It targets a namespace on the cluster where the workloads should live. The automated sync policy tells Argo to prune resources that were removed from Git and to self-heal any drift, so the cluster always matches what is committed.

scenes.text: Declare desired state in Git and let a controller reconcile it, then use canary or blue-green to release changes safely.
scenes.narration: The combined lesson is to declare your desired state in Git and let a controller reconcile it, then layer canary or blue-green strategies on top to release changes safely.
